clue.text: Wrote name again without protesting

definitions.meaning: to put one's signature on something a second time
accepting a situation meekly, with no complaint

explanation.surface: Someone signs a document a second time and raises no objection.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as RE-SIGNED it means signed once more; as one word it describes someone who accepts an unwelcome fate calmly.

clue.text: Salad ingredient, one added to bowl, following recipe

indicators.note: following here places the rest after the letter for recipe

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for recipe (from Latin recipe, take)
A means one, as in a single item
a bowl is a dish

explanation.surface: A cook adds an item to a bowl as the recipe instructs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following recipe' says A + DISH comes after R, the old prescription abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The small red root vegetable is a common raw addition to salads.

clue.text: Statute covering routes taken by planes in flights

indicators.note: in a down answer the piece covering another sits on top of it

parts.note: ST is an abbreviation for statute
aircraft fly along designated airways

explanation.surface: A law governing the paths that aircraft follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flights' looks aeronautical after 'planes', but it means flights of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a run of steps between floors, so stairways are flights.

clue.text: Fish-not sole, presumably

parts.note: playfully reads the fish's name as one who joins a group, so it would never be on its own, sole meaning alone as well as a flatfish

explanation.surface: A fish described as not being a flatfish.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large sea fish of the bass family; the clue jokes that its name means someone in a group.

clue.text: Almost first to leave, being in good time

indicators.note: first to leave says the opening letter of the word for almost departs

parts.note: almost means nearly

explanation.surface: Someone is nearly the first person to go home, arriving ahead of schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to leave' removes the opening N of NEARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Being early means arriving before the appointed hour, ahead of schedule.

clue.text: Manoeuvre essential to achieving ambition

indicators.note: essential to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A clever move is vital if you are to realise your aims.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambit is an opening ploy, a calculated move to gain advantage, as in chess.

clue.text: Doctor pays out for post mortem examination

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician hands over money for an examination of a corpse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun, but it is the verb signalling a rearrangement of PAYS OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: An autopsy is the medical examination of a body after death.

clue.text: British Labour leader heading a meeting with Irish?

definitions.text: British Labour leader heading a meeting with Irish?

indicators.note: leader here means only the opening letter of the word Labour is taken

explanation.surface: A UK Labour Party leader chairs a meeting with Irish politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: Every piece is spelt in order: B (British), L (Labour's leader), A, IR (Irish). The whole clue also describes Tony Blair, the Labour prime minister involved in Northern Irish peace talks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blair led the British Labour Party and was prime minister during the Good Friday Agreement talks with Irish leaders.

clue.text: Thinker tore this into bits

indicators.note: torn into bits means broken up, so these letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone rips this paper to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorist is someone who develops ideas and hypotheses, a thinker.

clue.text: Current equivalent of vest and long johns?

definitions.meaning: an undertow, a water current running below the surface

definitions.text: equivalent of vest and long johns?
definitions.meaning: a matching set of underclothes, playfully named

explanation.surface: A water current compared to a matching pair of thermal underclothes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a real term for a subsurface ocean current, and jokingly a set of underwear such as a vest with long johns.

clue.text: Have the lion's share of the business?

definitions.text: Have the lion's share of the business?

parts.words: Have the lion's share of the business?
parts.note: pictures a lion dominating a firm, while the idiom means a shop is busy and profitable, a lion's sound being part of the phrase

explanation.surface: A company's majority owner is asked about holding most of the trade.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to sell a great deal and prosper; a lion's roar makes the business literally roaring.

clue.text: Bolshie secret agent protects left during revolution

indicators.note: protects means the spy's letters surround and shelter another piece

parts.note: a secret agent is a spy

indicators.note: during revolution says the word for left is turned round

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A rebellious undercover operative shelters a left-winger amid an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: Port is the nautical word for left. Bolshie is British slang for difficult and uncooperative, from Bolshevik.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone bad-tempered and awkward, liable to throw a tantrum.

clue.text: Ruler's reputation in Italian city suffering setback

definitions.note: Ruler's stands for ruler is, the 's linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: a setback sends things backwards, so the assembled letters are read in the opposite direction
in places the word for reputation inside the city name

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital

explanation.surface: A leader's good name is damaged in an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering setback' reverses the whole assembled run, ROREPME, not just the city name.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is the sovereign of an empire, a supreme ruler.

clue.text: Forbid instruments of torture in military bases

parts.note: to bar is to forbid
racks were frames used to stretch victims

explanation.surface: Banning torture devices at army installations.
explanation.definitionFit: Barracks are the buildings where soldiers are housed, military quarters.

clue.text: Rubbish left frequently in attic room

parts.note: cock is British slang for nonsense, as in poppycock
oft is an old word for often

explanation.surface: Junk is often abandoned up in the loft.
explanation.walkthrough: COCK meaning nonsense is informal British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockloft is a small loft or garret at the top of a house.

clue.text: Tales, for instance, circulating about sailors

indicators.note: about places the reversed word around the sailors
circulating means going round, so the phrase for for instance is turned backwards

parts.note: say means for instance, as in a few, say three
RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors

explanation.surface: Stories, for example, being passed round about seafarers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulating' makes YAS; RN, the Royal Navy, is a standard crossword source for sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: A yarn is a long, often far-fetched story, especially a sailor's.

clue.text: Once again take transport round City of London

indicators.note: round means the word for transport goes around another piece

parts.note: transport in the sense of ecstasy is rapture
EC is the postcode district of the City of London

explanation.surface: Seizing a vehicle again around the financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' is not a vehicle but delight, RAPTURE; EC is the City of London's postcode prefix.
explanation.definitionFit: To recapture is to seize back, to take possession a second time.

clue.text: In a sense it's time to wait and see

indicators.note: In tells us the following pieces go inside the word for a sense

parts.note: sight is one of the five senses
it is taken as written, the 's being a link

explanation.surface: In a way, it's the moment to be patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a sense' looks like a hedging phrase, but 'In' is the container signal and 'a sense' the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stay put and take no action until things become clearer.

clue.text: Leaders of international standing confront Europe's recurring problem

indicators.note: leaders of means the opening letters of the next two words
recurring here means running back, so the letters for Europe's are reversed

parts.note: EU is the European Union, plus S from the possessive

explanation.surface: World leaders of high standing face Europe's persistent difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is a matter of concern or a point in dispute, a problem.

clue.text: Eliminate waste from holiday island

parts.note: ex means from, as in ex works
Crete is a popular Greek holiday island

explanation.surface: Removing rubbish from a tourist island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' looks like a link but supplies EX.
explanation.definitionFit: To excrete is to discharge bodily waste.

clue.text: Drop of water for eye problem

definitions.meaning: a large waterfall, where a river falls steeply
clouding of the lens causing blurred vision

explanation.surface: A drop of liquid prescribed for an eye condition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a great waterfall and the clouding of the eye's lens.

clue.text: Scottish writer given good grading

parts.note: Ian Rankin is a Scottish crime novelist

explanation.surface: A Scottish author receives a favourable assessment.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranking is a position in a graded order, so a grading.

clue.text: Here's endless source of sherry, my man

indicators.note: endless says the final letter of the place name is dropped

parts.note: Jerez in Spain gives sherry its name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man offers sherry from an inexhaustible supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the Z from JEREZ, the Andalusian town whose name became the word sherry.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy is a man's first name.

clue.text: Local coal pit in difficulty

indicators.note: in difficulty suggests the letters are in trouble and thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood coal mine is struggling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' looks like an adjective about the pit, but it is the definition in its medical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine a topical treatment is applied locally, to one part of the body.

clue.text: Dictator is someone lacking sensitivity for a start

indicators.note: lacking says a letter is missing from the word for someone

parts.note: someone is a person

indicators.note: for a start takes just the opening letter of sensitivity

explanation.surface: A tyrant is described as a callous individual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes S, the start of sensitivity, from PERSON. Juan Perón ruled Argentina.
explanation.definitionFit: Juan Perón was Argentina's authoritarian president, often called a dictator.

clue.text: Band of 120 Roman soldiers

parts.note: a plain description of a subdivision of a Roman legion, about a hundred and twenty men

explanation.surface: A description of a unit in the Roman army.
explanation.definitionFit: A maniple was a company of a Roman legion, made up of two centuries.

clue.text: Form of protest taking a few weeks?

definitions.meaning: a calendar month lasts four or so weeks

explanation.surface: A demonstration that drags on for several weeks.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a protest walk and the third month of the year.

clue.text: Perhaps picnic chairs ruined turf — anger erupts

indicators.note: erupts suggests the letters burst out and scatter into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Picnic chairs have damaged the lawn and someone loses their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder RUINED TURF ANGER, shuffled by 'erupts'.
explanation.definitionFit: Picnic chairs are one example of outdoor seating used in gardens.

clue.text: Sun cream for a few pence

definitions.meaning: a lotion that browns the skin
old slang for a sixpence coin

explanation.surface: Buying sun lotion for small change.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanner was the British sixpence, a coin worth six old pence.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a bronzing lotion and the old sixpenny coin.

clue.text: Attacker heading off, overwhelmed by your aggressive behaviour

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means the trimmed attacker is enclosed within the word for your

parts.note: thy is the old form of your

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter of the word for attacker goes

parts.note: a mugger attacks people in the street

explanation.surface: An assailant leaves, swamped by your violent conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops M from MUGGER, leaving UGGER, which THY surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Thuggery is violent, brutish conduct.
